title.zh: 卷四十 補列傳第三二 尉瑾 馮子琮 赫連子悅 唐邕 白建
title.en: Volume 40 Biographies 32: Yu Jin (Northern Qi); Feng Zicong; Helian Ziyue; Tang Yong; Bai Jian
title.raw: 卷四十 補列傳第三二 尉瑾 馮子琮 赫連子悅 唐邕 白建 Volume 40 Biographies 32: Yu Jin (Northern Qi); Feng Zicong; Helian Ziyue; Tang Yong; Bai Jian

sentences.zh: 尉瑾 馮子琮 赫連子悅 唐邕 白建

translations.literal: Yu Jin; Feng Zicong; Helian Ziyue; Tang Yong; Bai Jian
translations.idiomatic: Yu Jin; Feng Zicong; Helian Ziyue; Tang Yong; Bai Jian

sentences.zh: 尉瑾，字安仁。

translations.literal: Yu Jin, styled Anren.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Jin, styled Anren.

sentences.zh: 父慶賓，為魏肆州刺史。

translations.literal: His father Qingbin was Wei governor of Sizhou.
translations.idiomatic: His father Qingbin had been Wei governor of Sizhou.

sentences.zh: 瑾少而敏悟，好學慕善。

translations.literal: Jin from youth was quick and perceptive, loved learning, and admired goodness.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Jin was quick-witted, loved study, and sought what was good.

sentences.zh: 稍遷直後。

translations.literal: He was gradually promoted to straight attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He rose in turn to straight attendant.

sentences.zh: 司馬子如執政，瑾取其外生皮氏女，由此擢拜中書舍人。

translations.literal: When Sima Ziru held power, Jin took his maternal niece, daughter of the Pi clan, and was thereby promoted and appointed secretariat vice-director.
translations.idiomatic: When Sima Ziru held power, Jin married his maternal niece of the Pi clan and was promoted secretariat vice-director.

sentences.zh: 旣是子如姻戚，數往參詣，因與先達名輩微相款狎。

translations.literal: Being Ziru's affinal kin, he often went to call on him and thereby came to be on easy terms with eminent predecessors and noted men of the age.
translations.idiomatic: As Ziru's kin by marriage he often called on him and grew familiar with eminent elders and men of name.

sentences.zh: 世宗入朝，因命瑾在鄴北宮共高德正典機密。

translations.literal: When Gao Cheng entered the court, Jin was ordered to be at Ye's northern palace together with Gao Dezheng managing confidential affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Cheng came to court, Jin was ordered to Ye's northern palace to manage confidential affairs with Gao Dezheng.

sentences.zh: 肅宗輔政，累遷吏部尚書。

translations.literal: When Gao Yan assisted in government, Jin was repeatedly promoted to minister of personnel.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Yan assisted in government, Jin rose repeatedly to minister of personnel.

sentences.zh: 世祖踐祚，趙彥深本子如賓僚，元文遙、和士開並帝鄉故舊，共相薦達，任遇彌重。

translations.literal: When Gao Zhan ascended the throne, Zhao Yanshen had been a guest-officer of Ziru, Yuan Wenyao and He Shikai were all old acquaintances from the imperial hometown, and they jointly recommended and advanced him; his appointment and favor grew ever heavier.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Zhan took the throne, Zhao Yanshen had been Ziru's guest-officer, and Yuan Wenyao and He Shikai were all old friends from the imperial hometown. They recommended him together, and his rank and favor grew heavier still.

sentences.zh: 又吏部銓衡所歸，事多秘密，由是朝之幾事，頗亦預聞。

translations.literal: Moreover the personnel directorate's weighing and selection fell to him; affairs were mostly secret, and thereby he often heard beforehand of the court's weighty matters.
translations.idiomatic: Personnel weighing and selection also rested with him; much was secret, and so he often heard the court's weighty affairs in advance.

sentences.zh: 尋兼右僕射，攝選，未幾即真。

translations.literal: Soon he was additionally right vice director, acting in selection; before long he received the formal appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was also right vice director, acting in selection; before long the post was made formal.

sentences.zh: 病卒，世祖方在三臺飲酒，文遙奏聞，遂命徹樂罷飲。

translations.literal: He died of illness; Gao Zhan was at the time drinking at Santai; Wenyao reported it, and the emperor ordered music withdrawn and drinking stopped.
translations.idiomatic: He died of illness while Gao Zhan was drinking at Santai. Wenyao reported it, and the emperor ordered the music stopped and the drinking ended.

sentences.zh: 瑾外雖通顯，內闕風訓，閨門穢雜，為世所鄙。

translations.literal: Outwardly Jin was prominent, but inwardly his household lacked moral instruction; his inner chambers were foul and mixed, and the age despised him for it.
translations.idiomatic: Outwardly Jin was eminent, but at home he lacked moral discipline; his inner quarters were foul and disorderly, and the age despised him.

sentences.zh: 然亦能折節下士，意在引接名流，但不別之。

translations.literal: Yet he could also restrain himself and defer to scholars, meaning to draw in eminent men—but he did not distinguish them.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he could humble himself before scholars and meant to draw in men of name—only he could not tell them apart.

sentences.zh: 及官高任重，便大躁急，省內郎中將論事者逆即瞋詈，不可諮承。

translations.literal: When his office was high and his burden heavy, he became greatly impatient; within the ministry, those lang who wished to discuss affairs—if they went against him he would glare and curse at once, and they could not consult with him.
translations.idiomatic: Once rank and burden grew heavy he turned harsh and quick to anger. Within the ministry, any lang who came to discuss business and crossed him was glared at and cursed on the spot; none could seek his counsel.

sentences.zh: 旣居大選，彌自驕狠。

translations.literal: Once he held the great selection, he became all the more arrogant and harsh.
translations.idiomatic: Once he held the great selection he grew still more arrogant and cruel.

sentences.zh: 子德載嗣。

translations.literal: His son Dezai succeeded him.
translations.idiomatic: His son Dezai succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 馮子琮，信都人，北燕主馮跋之後也。

translations.literal: Feng Zicong, a man of Xindu, was a descendant of Northern Yan's ruler Feng Ba.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Zicong came from Xindu and was descended from Northern Yan's ruler Feng Ba.

sentences.zh: 父靈紹，度支郎中。

translations.literal: His father Lingshao was a lang in the revenue section.
translations.idiomatic: His father Lingshao was a lang in the revenue section.

sentences.zh: 子琮性聰敏，涉獵書傳。

translations.literal: Zicong was clever by nature and ranged through books and records.
translations.idiomatic: Zicong was clever by nature and read widely in books and records.

sentences.zh: 為。

translations.literal: He took office.
translations.idiomatic: He then entered official service.

sentences.zh: 肅宗除領軍府法曹，典機密，攝庫部。

translations.literal: Gao Yan appointed him to the staff bureau for law in the general-in-chief's office, managing confidential affairs and acting in the treasury section.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Yan made him law staff in the general-in-chief's office, put him in charge of confidential affairs, and had him act in the treasury section.

sentences.zh: 肅宗曾閱簿領，試令口陳，子琮闇對，無有遺失。

translations.literal: Gao Yan once reviewed ledgers; testing them, he had Zicong recite orally—and Zicong answered from memory without a single omission.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Yan once reviewed ledgers and tested Zicong by having him recite them aloud. Zicong answered from memory without missing a single entry.

sentences.zh: 子琮妻，胡皇后妹也。

translations.literal: Zicong's wife was the younger sister of the Hu empress.
translations.idiomatic: Zicong's wife was the Hu empress's younger sister.

sentences.zh: 遷殿中郎，加東宮管記。

translations.literal: He was promoted to attendant within the palace and additionally made eastern palace recorder.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted palace attendant and also made eastern palace recorder.

sentences.zh: 又奉別詔，令共胡長粲輔遵太子，轉庶子。

translations.literal: He was further given a separate edict to assist the crown prince together with Hu Changcai; he was transferred to subprefect of the heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: By a separate edict he was to assist the crown prince with Hu Changcai and was transferred to heir-apparent subprefect.

sentences.zh: 及世祖崩，僕射和士開先恒侍疾，秘喪三日不發。

translations.literal: When Gao Zhan died, Vice Director He Shikai had long attended his illness and kept the mourning secret for three days without announcing it.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Zhan died, vice director He Shikai had long attended his illness and kept the mourning secret for three days without announcing it.

sentences.zh: 子琮問士開不發喪之意。

translations.literal: Zicong asked He Shikai why he did not announce the mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Zicong asked He Shikai why he had not announced the mourning.

sentences.zh: 士開引神武、文襄初崩並秘喪不舉，至尊年少，恐王公有貳心，意欲普追集涼風堂，然後與詳議。

translations.literal: He Shikai cited that when Gao Huan and Gao Cheng first died, mourning was likewise kept secret; the sovereign was young and he feared the princes and dukes might harbor divided hearts; he intended to summon everyone to the Cool Breeze Hall and then discuss in detail.
translations.idiomatic: He Shikai said that when Gao Huan and Gao Cheng first died, mourning had likewise been kept secret. The sovereign was young; he feared the princes and dukes might waver, and meant to gather everyone at the Cool Breeze Hall before discussing matters in full.

sentences.zh: 時太尉錄尚書事趙郡王叡先恒居內，預帷幄之謀，子琮素知士開忌叡及領軍臨淮王婁定遠，恐其矯遺詔出叡外任，奪定遠禁衛之權，因答云：「大行，神武之子，今上又是先皇傳位，群臣富貴者皆是至尊父子之恩，但令在內貴臣一無改易，王公已下必無異望。

translations.literal: At the time Grand Mentor and Recorder of the Masters of Writing Affairs Prince of Zhao commandery Rui had long dwelt within the palace and took part in counsel at the curtain; Zicong had long known He Shikai resented Rui and General-in-Chief of the Guards Prince of Huai'nan Lou Dingyuan, and feared they might forge the final edict to send Rui out on external appointment and strip Dingyuan of guard authority; therefore he answered, saying, "The late emperor was Gao Huan's son, and the present sovereign likewise received the throne from the former emperor. Every minister's wealth and rank came from father and son's grace to the sovereign. If the honored men within the court are left wholly unchanged, the princes and dukes below will surely harbor no other intent.
translations.idiomatic: At the time grand mentor and recorder of the masters of writing affairs, Prince of Zhao commandery Rui, had long lived inside the palace and shared counsel at the curtain. Zicong knew He Shikai resented Rui and general-in-chief of the guards Prince of Huai'nan Lou Dingyuan and feared they might forge the final edict to send Rui out on provincial duty and strip Dingyuan of the guard command. He answered, "The late emperor was Gao Huan's son, and the present sovereign too received the throne from his predecessor. Every minister's wealth came from the sovereign father and son. Leave the great men inside the court unchanged, and the princes and dukes below will surely have no other wish.

sentences.zh: 世異事殊，不得與霸朝相比。

translations.literal: Times and affairs differ; this cannot be compared with the founding reign.
translations.idiomatic: "Times and affairs differ; this cannot be compared with the founding reign.

sentences.zh: 且公出宮門已經數日，升遐之事，行路皆傳，久而不舉，恐有他變。

translations.literal: Moreover, sir, you have been outside the palace gates already several days; news of the emperor's passing spreads on every road. If mourning is long delayed, I fear some other change may arise.
translations.idiomatic: "Moreover, sir, you have been outside the palace gates for days already, and news of the emperor's passing travels every road. Delay mourning too long and I fear some other turn may come.

sentences.zh: 」於是乃發喪。

translations.literal: " Thereupon mourning was announced.
translations.idiomatic: " Thereupon mourning was announced.

sentences.zh: 元文遙以子琮太后妹夫，恐其獎成太后干政，說趙郡王及士開出之，拜鄭州刺史，即令之任。

translations.literal: Yuan Wenyao, because Zicong was the empress's brother-in-law, feared he would encourage the empress to meddle in government; he persuaded Prince of Zhao commandery and He Shikai to send him out, appointed him governor of Zhengzhou, and ordered him to take up the post at once.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Wenyao, because Zicong was the empress's brother-in-law, feared he would encourage her to meddle in government. He persuaded Prince of Zhao commandery and He Shikai to send him out, made him governor of Zheng, and ordered him to take up the post at once.

sentences.zh: 子琮除州，非後主本意，中旨殷勤，特給後部鼓吹，加兵五十人，並聽將物度關。

translations.literal: Zicong's appointment to the province was not the Later Sovereign's original intent; the central edict was earnest and warm, and he was specially given rear guard musicians, fifty additional troops, and permission to bring goods across the passes.
translations.idiomatic: Zicong's provincial appointment was not what the Later Sovereign had first intended; the central edict was warm and earnest, and he was specially given rear guard musicians, fifty more troops, and leave to bring goods across the passes.

sentences.zh: 至州未幾，太后為齊安王納子琮長女為妃，子琮因請假赴鄴，遂授吏部尚書。

translations.literal: Not long after he reached the province, the empress dowager took Zicong's eldest daughter as consort for Prince of Qi'an; Zicong therefore asked leave to go to Ye and was then appointed minister of personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Not long after he reached the province, the empress dowager took Zicong's eldest daughter as consort for Prince of Qi'an. Zicong asked leave to go to Ye and was then made minister of personnel.

sentences.zh: 其妻恃親放縱，請謁公行，賄貨填積。

translations.literal: His wife relied on kinship and acted without restraint; requests and audiences went openly, and bribes piled up.
translations.idiomatic: His wife relied on kinship and acted without restraint; favors and audiences went openly, and bribes piled high.

sentences.zh: 守宰除授，先定錢帛多少，然後奏聞，其所通致，事無不允，子琮亦不禁制。

translations.literal: When prefects and magistrates were appointed, the amount of cash and silk was fixed first and only then reported to the throne; whatever they sought through him was never denied, and Zicong did not restrain it.
translations.idiomatic: For prefects and magistrates the price in cash and silk was fixed first and only then reported upward. Whatever they sought through him was granted, and Zicong did not restrain them.

sentences.zh: 俄遷尚書右僕射，仍攝選。

translations.literal: Before long he was promoted to right vice director of the masters of writing and still acted in selection.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was promoted right vice director of the masters of writing and still acted in selection.

sentences.zh: 和士開居要日久，子琮舊所附托，卑辭曲躬，事事諮稟。

translations.literal: He Shikai had long held a key post; Zicong had once relied on him and with humble words and bent body consulted him on every matter.
translations.idiomatic: He Shikai had long held power; Zicong had once relied on him, spoke humbly, bowed low, and consulted him on every matter.

sentences.zh: 士開弟休與盧氏婚，子琮檢校趨走，與士開府僚不異。

translations.literal: He Shikai's younger brother Xiu married into the Lu clan; Zicong attended and hurried about no differently from He Shikai's staff.
translations.idiomatic: He Shikai's younger brother Xiu married into the Lu clan; Zicong hurried about at the wedding no differently from He Shikai's own staff.

sentences.zh: 是時內官除授多由士開奏擬，子琮旣恃內戚，兼帶選曹，自擅權寵，頗生間隙。

translations.literal: At the time many inner appointments were proposed by He Shikai; Zicong, relying on inner kinship and also holding the selection office, monopolized favor and power, and friction arose.
translations.idiomatic: At the time many inner appointments came from He Shikai's proposals. Zicong, relying on inner kinship and also holding the selection office, monopolized favor and power, and friction grew between them.

sentences.zh: 瑯邪王儼殺士開，子琮與其事，就內省絞殺之。

translations.literal: Prince of Langye Yan killed He Shikai; Zicong took part in the affair and strangled him inside the inner secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Langye Yan killed He Shikai; Zicong took part in the affair and strangled him inside the inner secretariat.

sentences.zh: 子琮微有識鑒，及位望轉隆，宿心頓改。

translations.literal: Zicong had some discernment, but as rank and renown rose his long-held intent suddenly changed.
translations.idiomatic: Zicong had some discernment, but as rank and renown rose his old intent suddenly changed.

sentences.zh: 擢引非類，以為深交；

translations.literal: He promoted and drew in unworthy sorts and treated them as close friends;
translations.idiomatic: He promoted unworthy men and treated them as close friends;

sentences.zh: 縱其子弟，官位不依倫次；

translations.literal: he indulged his sons and younger brothers, giving offices out of proper order;
translations.idiomatic: he indulged his sons and younger brothers, giving offices out of proper order;

sentences.zh: 又專營婚媾，歷選上門，例以官爵許之，旬日便驗。

translations.literal: he also specialized in arranging marriages, choosing only great houses, and routinely promised office and rank; within ten days it was confirmed.
translations.idiomatic: he also specialized in arranging marriages, choosing only great houses, and routinely promised office and rank that were confirmed within ten days.

sentences.zh: 子慈正。

translations.literal: His son Cizheng.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Cizheng.

sentences.zh: 赫連子悅，字士欣，勃勃之後也。

translations.literal: Helian Ziyue, styled Shixin, was a descendant of Helian Bobo.
translations.idiomatic: Helian Ziyue, styled Shixin, was descended from Helian Bobo.

sentences.zh: 魏永安初，以軍功為濟州別駕。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yong'an under Wei he was made, for military merit, separate-assistant of Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In Wei's first Yong'an year he was made Jizhou separate-assistant for military merit.

sentences.zh: 及高祖起義，侯景為刺史，景本尒朱心腹，子悅勸景起義，景從之。

translations.literal: When Gao Huan raised the righteous army, Hou Jing was governor; Jing had originally been Erzhu Rong's trusted man, and Ziyue urged Jing to join the uprising; Jing followed him.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Huan raised the righteous army, Hou Jing was governor. Jing had been Erzhu Rong's trusted man; Ziyue urged him to join the uprising, and Jing followed.

sentences.zh: 除林慮守。

translations.literal: He was appointed defender of Linyu.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed defender of Linyu.

sentences.zh: 世宗往晉陽，路由是郡，因問所不便。

translations.literal: Gao Cheng was going to Jinyang and passed through that commandery; he therefore asked what was inconvenient.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Cheng was bound for Jinyang and passed through the commandery, so he asked what was inconvenient.

sentences.zh: 悅答云：「臨水、武安二縣去郡遙遠，山嶺重疊，車步艱難，若東屬魏郡，則地平路近。

translations.literal: Ziyue answered, saying, "The two counties of Linshui and Wu'an lie far from the commandery seat; mountains and ridges overlap, and cart and foot travel are hard. If they were attached east to Wei's commandery, the land would be level and the road near.
translations.idiomatic: Ziyue answered, "The counties of Linshui and Wu'an lie far from the seat; mountains pile up and travel by cart or on foot is hard. If they were placed under Wei's commandery to the east, the land would be level and the road short.

sentences.zh: 」世宗笑曰：「卿徒知便民，不覺損幹。

translations.literal: " Gao Cheng laughed and said, "You only know how to benefit the people and do not notice the harm to the trunk.
translations.idiomatic: " Gao Cheng laughed and said, "You only know how to ease the people and do not see the harm to the trunk.

sentences.zh: 」子悅答云：「所言因民疾苦，不敢以私潤負心。

translations.literal: Ziyue answered, saying, "What I spoke of follows the people's hardship; I dare not let private gain outweigh my heart.
translations.idiomatic: Ziyue answered, "What I said follows the people's hardship; I dare not let private gain outweigh my heart.

sentences.zh: 」世宗云：「卿能如此，甚善甚善。

translations.literal: " Gao Cheng said, "You can be like this—very good, very good.
translations.idiomatic: " Gao Cheng said, "You can be like this—excellent, excellent.

sentences.zh: 」仍勑依事施行。

translations.literal: " He then ordered it carried out according to the proposal.
translations.idiomatic: " He then ordered the change carried out as proposed.

sentences.zh: 在郡滿，更徵為臨漳令。

translations.literal: When his term in the commandery was complete, he was summoned again as magistrate of Linzhang.
translations.idiomatic: When his commandery term ended he was summoned again as magistrate of Linzhang.

sentences.zh: 後除鄭州刺史，于時新經河清大水，民多逃散，子悅親加恤隱，戶口益增，治為天下之最。

translations.literal: Later he was made governor of Zhengzhou; at the time the region had just suffered the great flood of the Heqing era, and the people had fled in great numbers; Ziyue personally went to comfort and shelter them, households increased, and his governance ranked first in the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was made governor of Zheng. The region had just suffered the Heqing great flood; many people had fled. Ziyue went in person to comfort them, households increased, and his governance ranked first in the realm.

sentences.zh: 入為都官尚書，鄭州民八百餘請立碑頌德，有詔許焉。

translations.literal: He entered court as director of the ministry of justice; more than eight hundred men of Zhengzhou asked to erect a stele praising his virtue, and an edict permitted it.
translations.idiomatic: He entered court as director of the ministry of justice. More than eight hundred men of Zheng asked to raise a stele praising his virtue, and an edict permitted it.

sentences.zh: 後以本官兼吏部。

translations.literal: Later, in his original office, he was additionally made acting in the personnel directorate.
translations.idiomatic: Later, while keeping his original office, he was additionally made acting in the personnel directorate.

sentences.zh: 子悅在官，唯以清勤自守，旣無學術，又闕風儀，人倫清鑒，去之彌遠，一旦居銓衡之首，大招物議。

translations.literal: Ziyue in office relied only on purity and diligence to hold himself; he had neither learning nor bearing, and in human discernment he fell ever farther away—yet once he stood at the head of weighing and selection, he drew great criticism from the age.
translations.idiomatic: In office Ziyue held himself only by purity and diligence. He had neither learning nor bearing, and in judging men he fell ever farther short—yet once he stood at the head of weighing and selection, he drew heavy criticism.

sentences.zh: 由是除太常卿，卒。

translations.literal: Thereupon he was made director of the ministry of rites and died.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he was made director of the ministry of rites and died.

sentences.zh: 唐邕，字道和，太原晉陽人，其先自晉昌徙焉。

translations.literal: Tang Yong, styled Daohe, was a man of Jinyang in Taiyuan; his ancestors had moved there from Jinchang.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Yong, styled Daohe, came from Jinyang in Taiyuan; his ancestors had moved there from Jinchang.

sentences.zh: 父靈芝，魏壽陽令。

translations.literal: His father Lingzhi was Wei magistrate of Shouyang.
translations.idiomatic: His father Lingzhi was Wei magistrate of Shouyang.

sentences.zh: 邕少明敏，有治世才具。

translations.literal: Yong from youth was bright and keen and had the talent and equipment to order an age.
translations.idiomatic: Yong was bright and keen from youth and had the talent to order an age.

sentences.zh: 太昌初，或薦於高祖，命其直外兵曹，典執文帳。

translations.literal: In the first year of Taichang someone recommended him to Gao Huan; Gao Huan ordered him to attend the outer military affairs bureau and manage written registers.
translations.idiomatic: In the first Taichang year someone recommended him to Gao Huan, who had him attend the outer military affairs bureau and manage written registers.

sentences.zh: 邕善書計，強記默識，以幹濟見知，擢為世宗大將軍府參軍。

translations.literal: Yong was skilled at reckoning and accounts, had a strong memory and silent retention, and was known for practical ability; he was promoted staff officer in Gao Cheng's grand general's office.
translations.idiomatic: Yong was skilled at reckoning and accounts, remembered silently, and was known for practical ability. He was promoted staff officer in Gao Cheng's grand general's office.

sentences.zh: 及世宗崩，事出倉卒，顯祖部分將士，鎮壓四方，夜中召邕支配，造次便了，顯祖甚重之。

translations.literal: When Gao Cheng died, affairs arose in sudden haste; Gao Yang deployed the generals and soldiers and suppressed the four quarters; in the night he summoned Yong to arrange matters, and at once it was done—Gao Yang valued him greatly.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Cheng died, affairs broke out in haste. Gao Yang deployed generals and soldiers to hold the four quarters, summoned Yong at night to arrange matters, and at once it was done. Gao Yang valued him greatly.

sentences.zh: 顯祖頻年出塞，邕必陪從，專掌兵機。

translations.literal: Gao Yang year after year went beyond the frontier; Yong always accompanied him and specialized in military plans.
translations.idiomatic: Year after year Gao Yang went beyond the frontier; Yong always accompanied him and specialized in military plans.

sentences.zh: 識悟閑明，承受敏速，自督將以還，軍吏以上，勞效由緒，無不諳練，每有顧問，占對如響。

translations.literal: His discernment was clear and unhurried, his reception quick; from supervising generals down, and military clerks and above, merit and service followed the thread and none was unfamiliar—whenever there was inquiry, his reply came like an echo.
translations.idiomatic: His discernment was clear and unhurried, his reception quick. From supervising generals down and army clerks up, merit and service followed the thread and none was unfamiliar; whenever he was asked, he answered like an echo.

sentences.zh: 或於御前簡閱，雖三五千人，邕多不執文簿，暗唱官位姓名，未常謬誤。

translations.literal: Sometimes before the emperor he would review troops; though three to five thousand men, Yong often held no ledger and would recite in the dark their offices, ranks, and names, and never erred.
translations.idiomatic: Sometimes the emperor reviewed troops before him; though three or five thousand men, Yong often held no ledger and recited office, rank, and name from memory without error.

sentences.zh: 七年，於羊汾堤講武，令邕總為諸軍節度。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, at the Yangfen embankment he lectured on military affairs and ordered Yong to command the discipline of all armies.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year, at the Yangfen embankment, he lectured on military affairs and ordered Yong to command discipline for all armies.

sentences.zh: 事畢，仍監宴射之禮。

translations.literal: When the affair was finished, he still oversaw the ritual of the review feast and archery.
translations.idiomatic: When the affair ended he still oversaw the review feast and archery ritual.

sentences.zh: 是日，顯祖親執邕手，引至太后前，坐於丞相斛律金之上，啟太后云：「唐邕強幹，一人當千。

translations.literal: That day Gao Yang personally took Yong's hand, led him before the empress dowager, seated him above Chancellor Hulü Jin, and told the empress dowager, saying, "Tang Yong is strong and capable—one man equals a thousand.
translations.idiomatic: That day Gao Yang took Yong's hand, led him before the empress dowager, seated him above chancellor Hulü Jin, and told her, "Tang Yong is strong and capable—one man equals a thousand.

sentences.zh: 」仍別賜錦彩錢帛。

translations.literal: " He then separately bestowed brocade, silk, cash, and goods.
translations.idiomatic: " He then separately bestowed brocade, silk, cash, and goods.

sentences.zh: 邕非唯強濟明辨，然亦善揣上意，進取多途，是以恩寵日隆，委任彌重。

translations.literal: Yong was not only strong, capable, bright, and discerning; he also knew how to gauge the sovereign's intent, and his paths of advancement were many—therefore favor daily grew and commission grew ever heavier.
translations.idiomatic: Yong was not only strong, capable, bright, and discerning; he also knew how to read the sovereign's intent and had many paths of advance, so favor grew daily and commission grew heavier.

sentences.zh: 顯祖又嘗對邕白太后云：「唐邕分明強記，每有軍機大事，手作文書，口且處分，耳又聽受，實是異人。

translations.literal: Gao Yang also once said to Yong before the empress dowager, "Tang Yong distinguishes clearly and remembers strongly; whenever there is a weighty military affair, he writes documents by hand, gives orders by mouth, and listens with his ear at the same time—truly a different man.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Yang also once told the empress dowager before Yong, "Tang Yong distinguishes clearly and remembers strongly. On great military affairs he writes documents by hand, gives orders by mouth, and listens with his ear at once—truly a different man.

sentences.zh: 」一日之中，六度賜物。

translations.literal: " In a single day he was six times given gifts.
translations.idiomatic: " In a single day he was given gifts six times.

sentences.zh: 又嘗解所服青鼠皮裘賜邕，云：「朕意在車馬衣裘與卿共弊。

translations.literal: He also once removed the blue sable fur coat he was wearing and bestowed it on Yong, saying, "My intent is that carriages, horses, clothes, and furs be worn out together with you.
translations.idiomatic: He also once removed the blue sable coat he was wearing and gave it to Yong, saying, "My intent is that carriages, horses, clothes, and furs be worn out together with you.

sentences.zh: 」十年，從幸晉陽，除兼給事黃門侍郎，領中書舍人。

translations.literal: " In the tenth year, accompanying the imperial progress to Jinyang, he was made acting attendant of the yellow gate and leading secretariat vice-director.
translations.idiomatic: " In the tenth year, on the progress to Jinyang, Yong was made acting attendant of the yellow gate and leading secretariat vice-director.

sentences.zh: 顯祖嘗登童子佛寺，望幷州城曰：「此是何等城？

translations.literal: Gao Yang once ascended the Tongzi Buddhist temple, looked toward Bingzhou city, and said, "What sort of city is this?
translations.idiomatic: Gao Yang once climbed Tongzi Buddhist temple, looked toward Bingzhou city, and said, "What sort of city is this?

sentences.zh: 」或曰：「此是金城湯池，天府之國。

translations.literal: " Someone said, "This is a metal rampart and boiling moat, a realm of heaven's storehouse.
translations.idiomatic: " Someone said, "This is a metal rampart and boiling moat—the realm's heavenly storehouse.

sentences.zh: 」帝云：「我謂唐邕是金城，此非金城也。

translations.literal: " The emperor said, "I say Tang Yong is the metal rampart; this is not the metal rampart.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said, "I say Tang Yong is the metal rampart; this is not the metal rampart.

sentences.zh: 」其見重如此。

translations.literal: " Such was the weight in which he was held.
translations.idiomatic: " Such was the weight in which he was held.

sentences.zh: 其後語邕曰：「卿劬勞旣久，欲除卿作州，頻勑楊遵彥更求一人堪代卿者。

translations.literal: Afterward he said to Yong, "Your toil has been long; I wished to make you governor of a province and repeatedly ordered Yang Zunyan to find another man who could replace you.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward he said to Yong, "Your toil has been long. I wished to make you governor of a province and repeatedly ordered Yang Zunyan to find another man who could replace you.

sentences.zh: 遵彥云比遍訪文武，如卿之徒實不可得，所以遂停此意。

translations.literal: Zunyan said that having searched everywhere among civil and military men, men like you truly cannot be obtained, and so this intent was stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Zunyan said that having searched civil and military men everywhere, a man like you truly cannot be found, and so this intent was stopped.

sentences.zh: 卿宜勉之。

translations.literal: You should strive on.
translations.idiomatic: You should strive on.

sentences.zh: 」顯祖或時切責侍臣不稱旨者：「觀卿等舉措，不中與唐邕作奴。

translations.literal: Gao Yang sometimes sharply rebuked attending ministers who did not suit his intent: "Watch how you comport yourselves—you are not fit to be Tang Yong's slaves.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Yang sometimes sharply rebuked attending ministers who missed his intent: "Watch how you comport yourselves—you are not fit to be Tang Yong's slaves.

sentences.zh: 」其見賞遇多此類。

translations.literal: " His favor and treatment were mostly of this sort.
translations.idiomatic: " His favor and treatment were mostly of this sort.

sentences.zh: 肅宗作相，除黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: When Gao Yan was made chief minister, Yong was made attendant of the yellow gate.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Yan was made chief minister, Yong was made attendant of the yellow gate.

sentences.zh: 於華林園射，特賜金帶寶器服玩雜物五百種。

translations.literal: At the Hualin Garden archery review he was specially given five hundred kinds of gold belts, precious vessels, robes, playthings, and miscellaneous goods.
translations.idiomatic: At the Hualin Garden archery review he was specially given five hundred kinds of gold belts, precious vessels, robes, playthings, and miscellaneous goods.

sentences.zh: 天統初，除侍中、幷州大中正，又拜護軍，餘如故。

translations.literal: Early in Tiantong he was made regular attendant and great rectifier of Bingzhou, and again appointed general of the guards; the rest of his offices remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Tiantong he was made regular attendant and great rectifier of Bing, and again appointed general of the guards; the rest of his offices remained as before.

sentences.zh: 邕以軍民教習田獵，依令十二月，月別三圍，以為人馬疲敝，奏請每月兩圍。

translations.literal: Yong, because military and civilian instruction in field hunts followed the statute of the twelfth month with three hunts each month, thought men and horses were worn out and memorialized asking for two hunts each month.
translations.idiomatic: Yong thought military and civilian field-hunt instruction, which by statute ran three hunts each month in the twelfth month, wore out men and horses, and memorialized for two hunts each month.

sentences.zh: 世祖從之。

translations.literal: Gao Zhan followed it.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Zhan approved it.

sentences.zh: 後出為趙州刺史，餘官如故。

translations.literal: Later he went out as governor of Zhao province; his other offices remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: Later he went out as governor of Zhao; his other offices remained as before.

sentences.zh: 世祖謂邕曰：「朝臣未有帶侍中、護軍、中正作州者，以卿故有此舉，放卿百餘日休息，至秋間當即追卿。

translations.literal: Gao Zhan said to Yong, "No court minister has yet held regular attendant, general of the guards, and great rectifier while serving as governor; this appointment is because of you. I give you more than a hundred days' rest; in autumn I shall recall you at once.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Zhan said to Yong, "No court minister has yet held regular attendant, general of the guards, and great rectifier while serving as governor; this move is because of you. I give you more than a hundred days' rest; in autumn I shall recall you at once.

sentences.zh: 」遷右僕射，又遷尚書令，封晉昌王，錄尚書事。

translations.literal: He was transferred to right vice director, then again to director of the masters of writing, enfeoffed as Prince of Jinchang, and made recorder of the masters of writing affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to right vice director, then again to director of the masters of writing, enfeoffed as Prince of Jinchang, and made recorder of the masters of writing affairs.

sentences.zh: 屬周師來寇，丞相高阿那肱率兵赴援，邕配割不甚從允，因此有隙。

translations.literal: As Zhou troops came to raid, Chancellor Gao Anaigong led troops to the relief; Yong's allocations and distributions were not fully approved, and on this account a rift opened.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhou troops came to raid, Chancellor Gao Anaigong led an army to relieve the siege; Tang Yong's supply allotments were not fully approved, and the two fell out.

sentences.zh: 肱譖之，遣侍中斛律孝卿宣旨責讓，留身禁止，尋釋之。

translations.literal: Anaigong slandered him and sent Attendant-in-Ordinary Hulu Xiaoxiaoqing to proclaim an edict rebuking and reproaching him; Yong was detained in custody and soon released.
translations.idiomatic: Anaigong slandered him and sent Attendant-in-Ordinary Hulu Xiaoxiaoqing with an edict of rebuke; Tang Yong was held in custody, then soon released.

sentences.zh: 車駕將幸晉陽，勑孝卿總知騎兵度支，事多自決，不相詢稟。

translations.literal: As the imperial carriage was about to visit Jinyang, an edict ordered Xiaoxiaoqing to take overall charge of cavalry expenditures; he decided most matters on his own and did not consult or report upward.
translations.idiomatic: As the emperor was about to visit Jinyang, an edict put Hulu Xiaoxiaoqing in overall charge of cavalry expenditures; he decided most matters himself and did not consult or report upward.

sentences.zh: 邕自恃從霸朝以來常典樞要，歷事六帝，恩遇甚重，一旦為孝卿所輕，負氣鬱怏，形於辭色。

translations.literal: Yong relied on himself—from the hegemonic court onward he had constantly held pivotal posts, served six emperors, and received very heavy favor—yet was suddenly slighted by Xiaoxiaoqing; resentful and sullen, he showed it in word and countenance.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Yong relied on having held pivotal posts since the hegemonic court, served six emperors, and enjoyed heavy favor—yet was suddenly slighted by Xiaoxiaoqing; bitter and sullen, he showed it in speech and face.

sentences.zh: 帝平陽敗後，狼狽還鄴都。

translations.literal: After the emperor's defeat at Pingyang, he returned to the capital Ye in disarray.
translations.idiomatic: After the emperor's defeat at Pingyang, he fled back to Ye in disarray.

sentences.zh: 邕懼那肱譖之，恨斛律孝卿輕己，遂留晉陽，與莫多婁敬顯等崇樹安德王為帝。

translations.literal: Yong feared Anaigong would slander him again and hated that Hulu Xiaoxiaoqing slighted him; he therefore remained at Jinyang and, with Moduolou Jingxian and others, elevated the Prince of Ande as emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Yong feared Anaigong would slander him again and resented Hulu Xiaoxiaoqing's slight; he stayed at Jinyang and, with Moduolou Jingxian and others, elevated the Prince of Ande as emperor.

sentences.zh: 信宿城陷，邕遂降周，依例授儀同大將軍。

translations.literal: Within a day or two the city fell; Yong then surrendered to Zhou and was appointed, by precedent, Pillar of State and Grand General.
translations.idiomatic: Within a day or two the city fell; Tang Yong surrendered to Zhou and, by precedent, was made Pillar of State and grand general.

sentences.zh: 卒於鳳州刺史。

translations.literal: He died while serving as governor of Feng Province.
translations.idiomatic: He died as governor of Feng Province.

sentences.zh: 邕性識明敏，通解時事，齊氏一代，典執兵機。

translations.literal: Yong was by nature intelligent and keen, understood current affairs, and throughout the Northern Qi line held command of military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Yong was intelligent and keen by nature, understood current affairs, and throughout Northern Qi held command of military affairs.

sentences.zh: 凡是九州軍士、四方勇募，強弱多少，番代往還，及器械精粗、糧儲虛實，精心勤事，莫不諳知。

translations.literal: All troops of the nine provinces, valiant recruits from the four quarters, their strength and numbers, rotations coming and going, and the fineness of weapons and fullness or emptiness of grain stores—he worked at these with keen care and knew them all thoroughly.
translations.idiomatic: Troops of the nine provinces, valiant recruits from the four quarters, their strength and numbers, rotations, the quality of weapons, and the state of grain stores—he tracked all of it with keen care and knew it thoroughly.

sentences.zh: 自大寧以來，奢侈糜費，比及武平之末，府藏漸虛。

translations.literal: From the Daning era onward luxury and waste ran rampant; by the end of Wuping the treasury stores were gradually depleted.
translations.idiomatic: From the Daning era on, luxury and waste ran rampant; by the end of Wuping the treasury was gradually empty.

sentences.zh: 邕度支取捨，大有裨益。

translations.literal: Yong's revenue decisions in expenditure brought great benefit.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Yong's revenue and expenditure decisions brought great benefit.

sentences.zh: 然旣被任遇，意氣漸高，其未經府寺陳訴，越覽詞牒，條數甚多，俱為憲臺及左丞彈糾，並御注放免。

translations.literal: Yet once favored in appointment his spirit grew gradually haughty; many cases in which he had not lodged petitions through the departmental offices but reviewed memorials on his own authority were impeached by the Censorate and the left vice-director—all were pardoned by imperial annotation.
translations.idiomatic: Yet once in favor his pride grew; many times he reviewed memorials without going through the offices, and the Censorate and left vice-director impeached him—all were pardoned by imperial note.

sentences.zh: 司空從事中郎封長業、太尉記室參軍平濤並為徵官錢違限，邕各杖背二十。

translations.literal: Attendant of the Ministry of Works Feng Changye and secretary of the Grand Commandant's office Ping Tao both exceeded the limit on recruitment money; Yong had each beaten on the back twenty strokes.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Changye, attendant of the Ministry of Works, and Ping Tao, secretary in the Grand Commandant's office, both exceeded the recruitment-money limit; Tang Yong had each flogged on the back twenty strokes.

sentences.zh: 齊時宰相未有撾撻朝士者，至是甚駭物聽。

translations.literal: In Qi times no chancellor had yet beaten or flogged court gentlemen; at this the court was greatly shocked.
translations.idiomatic: In Qi no chancellor had yet beaten a court gentleman; this greatly shocked public opinion.

sentences.zh: 邕三子。

translations.literal: Yong had three sons.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Yong had three sons.

sentences.zh: 長子君明，開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: His eldest son Junming held the rank Opening Ritual, Equal to the Three Dukes.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Junming held the rank opening ritual, equal to the three dukes.

sentences.zh: 開皇初，卒於應州刺史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Sui's Kaihuang era he died as governor of Ying Province.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Sui's Kaihuang era he died as governor of Ying Province.

sentences.zh: 次子君徹，中書舍人，隋順、戎二州刺史，大業中，卒於武賁郎將。

translations.literal: His second son Junche was secretariat gentleman; he served as governor of the two Sui provinces Shun and Rong; in the Daye era he died as martial guard commandant.
translations.idiomatic: His second son Junche was a secretariat gentleman and governor of Shun and Rong under Sui; in the Daye era he died as martial guard commandant.

sentences.zh: 少子君德，以邕降周伏法。

translations.literal: His youngest son Junde was executed by law because Yong had surrendered to Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: His youngest son Junde was executed because Tang Yong had surrendered to Zhou.

sentences.zh: 齊朝因高祖作相，丞相府外兵曹、騎兵曹分掌兵馬。

translations.literal: In Northern Qi, because the Grand Ancestor was made chancellor, the Grand Chancellor's office external military bureau and cavalry bureau divided control of troops and horses.
translations.idiomatic: In Northern Qi, when the Grand Ancestor became chancellor, the grand chancellor's external military bureau and cavalry bureau divided control of troops and horses.

sentences.zh: 及天保受禪，諸司監咸歸尚書，唯此二曹不廢，令唐邕、白建主治，謂之外兵省、騎兵省。

translations.literal: When Tianbao received the mandate, all office supervisors were folded into the Masters of Writing, but these two bureaus were not abolished; Tang Yong and Bai Jian were put in charge of them, called the External Troops Department and Cavalry Department.
translations.idiomatic: When Tianbao received the mandate, all office supervisors went to the Masters of Writing, but these two bureaus remained; Tang Yong and Bai Jian headed them, called the External Troops Department and Cavalry Department.

sentences.zh: 其後邕、建位望轉隆，各為省主，令中書舍人分判二省事，故世稱唐、白云。

translations.literal: Later Yong and Jian's standing grew ever loftier; each became head of his department; secretariat gentlemen were assigned to divide decisions on the two departments' affairs—hence the age called them Tang and Bai.
translations.idiomatic: Later Yong and Jian rose higher; each became head of his department, with secretariat gentlemen to divide their affairs—hence the age called them Tang and Bai.

sentences.zh: 白建，字彥舉，太原陽邑人也。

translations.literal: Bai Jian, styled Yansu, was a native of Yangyi in Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Bai Jian, styled Yansu, was from Yangyi in Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 初入大丞相府騎兵曹，典執文帳，明解書計，為同局所推。

translations.literal: He first entered the Grand Chancellor's office cavalry bureau, kept charge of clerical registers, understood bookkeeping clearly, and was pushed forward by colleagues in the same office.
translations.idiomatic: He first entered the grand chancellor's cavalry bureau, kept the clerical registers, understood accounts, and was promoted by colleagues in the same office.

sentences.zh: 天保十年，兼中書舍人。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Tianbao he was additionally made secretariat gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year of Tianbao he was additionally made secretariat gentleman.

sentences.zh: 肅宗輔政，除大丞相騎兵參軍。

translations.literal: When Suzong was regent he was appointed grand chancellor's office cavalry adjutant.
translations.idiomatic: When Suzong was regent he was appointed cavalry adjutant in the grand chancellor's office.

sentences.zh: 河清三年，突厥入境，代、忻二牧悉是細馬，合數萬匹，在五臺山北栢谷中避賊。

translations.literal: In the third year of Heqing, when the Turks invaded the border, the Dai and Xin herds were all fine horses, numbering tens of thousands together; they sheltered from bandits in Cypress Valley north of Mount Wutai.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Heqing, when Turks raided the border, the Dai and Xin herds—all fine horses, tens of thousands together—hid from bandits in Cypress Valley north of Mount Wutai.

sentences.zh: 賊退後，勑建就彼檢校，續使人詣建間領馬，送定州付民養飼。

translations.literal: After the bandits retreated, an edict ordered Jian to go there and inspect; messengers were continually sent to Jian to take over the horses and deliver them to Ding Province to be given to the people for raising and feeding.
translations.idiomatic: After the raiders withdrew, an edict sent Jian to inspect; messengers kept coming for him to take the horses and send them to Ding Province for the people to raise.

sentences.zh: 建以馬久不得食，瘦弱，遠送恐多死損，遂違勑以便宜從事，隨近散付軍人。

translations.literal: Jian judged that the horses had long gone without food and were emaciated; sending them far he feared many would die in transit; he therefore disobeyed the edict and acted on expedient grounds, dispersing and entrusting them nearby to soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Jian judged the horses had long gone unfed and were thin; a long haul would kill many, so he disobeyed the edict, acted as expedient required, and distributed them nearby to soldiers.

sentences.zh: 啟知，勑許焉。

translations.literal: He reported and the emperor learned; an edict permitted it.
translations.idiomatic: He reported; the emperor learned and approved by edict.

sentences.zh: 戎乘無損，建有力焉。

translations.literal: The war horses suffered no loss—Jian had merit in this.
translations.idiomatic: The war horses suffered no loss—Jian had credit for this.

sentences.zh: 武平末，歷特進、侍中、中書令。

translations.literal: At the end of Wuping he rose through special advance, attendant-in-ordinary, and chief minister of the secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Wuping he rose through special advance, attendant-in-ordinary, and chief minister of the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 建雖無他才，勤於在公。

translations.literal: Jian had no other talent but was diligent in public duty.
translations.idiomatic: Jian had no other talent but was diligent in public affairs.

sentences.zh: 屬王業始基，戎寄為重，建與唐邕俱以典執兵馬致位卿相。

translations.literal: As the royal enterprise was just beginning and military trust was weighty, Jian and Tang Yong both rose to minister and chancellor by keeping charge of troops and horses.
translations.idiomatic: As the royal enterprise was just beginning and military trust was weighty, Jian and Tang Yong both reached minister and chancellor by holding charge of troops and horses.

sentences.zh: 晉陽，國之下都，每年臨幸，徵詔差科，責成州郡。

translations.literal: Jinyang was the realm's lower capital; each year the emperor visited it; levies and corvée were dispatched, responsibility fixed on the provinces and commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: Jinyang was the realm's lower capital; each year the emperor visited, and levies and corvée fell on the provinces and commanderies.

sentences.zh: 本藩僚佐爰及守宰，諮承陳請，趨走無暇。

translations.literal: Retainers and administrators of his original domain, and even district magistrates, came to consult and present requests—they had no leisure to rest.
translations.idiomatic: Retainers and magistrates of his original domain came to consult and petition—they had no rest.

sentences.zh: 諸子幼稚，俱為州郡主簿，新君選補，必先召辟。

translations.literal: Though his sons were still young, all became chief clerks in the provinces and commanderies; when the new ruler chose and appointed, they were always summoned and engaged first.
translations.idiomatic: Though his sons were still young, all became provincial chief clerks; when the new ruler made appointments, they were always summoned first.

sentences.zh: 男婚女嫁，皆得勝流。

translations.literal: When sons married and daughters wed, they all won eminent company.
translations.idiomatic: Sons' marriages and daughters' weddings all matched leading families.

sentences.zh: 當世以為榮寵之極。

translations.literal: The age regarded this as the summit of honor and favor.
translations.idiomatic: The age took this as the height of honor and favor.

sentences.zh: 武平七年卒。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Wuping he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Wuping he died.

sentences.zh: 全文以中華書局、一九七二年十一月、第一版《北齊書》為本校。

translations.literal: The full text uses the Zhonghua Shuju first edition of the Book of Northern Qi (November 1972) as the base for collation.
translations.idiomatic: The full text uses the Zhonghua Shuju first edition of the Book of Northern Qi (November 1972) as the base for collation.
